messages:
maria: Heads up, saw an incident this morning where slow client heartbeats + proxy backpressure caused immediate reconnect storms. Console showed two 'active' sessions for the same client and billing doubled for ~2m.

jin: Oof. Is this the scenario where the proxy returns 204/keepalive while the backend is slow and client thinks it's disconnected?

maria: Exactly. Sequence: backend stall -> proxy holds socket open with empty keepalives -> client misses application-level chunk for 5s, triggers reconnect logic -> new session attaches while old socket still considered live by proxy -> resume succeeds and tokens get billed twice.

kevin: From console side we only reconcile by session_id; in this case resume used a new resume id so UI treated it as a second session. We probably need a better signal to mark old session as superseded.

olivia: Any traces? logs or sample headers would help. Might be able to correlate with proxy L7 idle timeouts.

maria: I've pasted a minimal repro trace (sanitized):

```
PROXY: keepalive sent at t+0, backend stalled
CLIENT: no application chunk by t+5 -> reconnect
PROXY: old socket still ESTABLISHED, resume token accepted for new socket
BILLING: tokens emitted for both sockets from t+5..t+125
```

jin: Two angles: make resume idempotent so resume on a new socket invalidates the old one server-side; and make proxy actively close old session on resume acceptance to avoid double billing.

kevin: UX angle: console should show an aggregation view that binds by client_id or request_id, and flag overlapping sessions as "suspected duplicate". Right now it's easy to misread as two users.

maria: Agreed. Quick mitigation: server-side check on resume that checks last_active_ts and if a newer resume exists, reject or accept with a note to close previous. But we also need to avoid breaking legitimate multi-device resumes.

jin: We can add a small TTL window where resume is accepted but sends a control event to proxy to terminate previous connection. Proposed flow: resume -> backend validates token -> emits control message to proxy with old_socket_id -> proxy sends FIN. That should be quick.

olivia: How reliable is proxy control plane messaging? We need to be sure this won't race and leak billing still. If the proxy control fails, we need fallback.

maria: Fallback: if control plane doesn't acknowledge, backend marks both sockets as candidate duplicate and disables billing for the older one retroactively (emit compensating credit). Not great but acceptable short-term.

kevin: Console should consume the duplicate marker and surface a timeline with an action like "merge sessions" or "refund overlap" for ops. Also add a sampling metric: percent of sessions with overlapping active windows > Xs.

jin: Implementation tasks: (1) add resume handshake that includes old_socket_id; (2) proxy control endpoint to kill socket; (3) backend atomic resume acceptance + emit control; (4) billing dedupe logic that prefers latest accepted resume.

maria: Also add telemetry: emit events (resume_attempt, resume_accept, old_socket_killed, overlap_detected) with trace_id to tie them together. We lack a few of these today so that's why this slipped past alerts.

olivia: I'll add an alert rule to detect "overlap_detected" rate spike in the short term. Set threshold low (0.1% of streaming sessions) and page on sustained >1% for 5m.

kevin: Console UX: show a small badge "duplicate resume suspected" and a link to the session trace. We already have trace links, just add the badge when overlap flag present.

maria: Any objections to a canary rollout? I'd like to ship resume control plane + proxy termination as canary to us-east and test with synthetic clients.

jin: No objections. I'll own the runtime change. Plan: feature-flag resume-control, proxy accepts control messages only when flag on.

olivia: I'll coordinate canary alerting and SLO slack channel.

kevin: I'll prepare a console patch behind a feature flag that surfaces the badge and links but hidden by default.

maria: Timeline? Can we get an initial canary by EOD Friday?

jin: EOD Friday for a basic resume-control PR + proxy endpoint. Canary deploy early next week after QA.

olivia: I'll schedule smoke tests and add the alerting rule.

maria: Cool. Action items summary: 
- jin: PR for resume handshake + proxy control (feature-flagged)
- kevin: console badge + merge action (feature-flagged)
- olivia: alerting, smoke tests, SLO channel
- maria: write postmortem note and coordinate billing dedupe fallback

kevin: Quick question — do we need to touch billing pipeline schema? retro credits are ugly. Could we avoid credits by marking older socket as free immediately on resume accept?

maria: That's the goal but we're not 100% certain the proxy will close immediately; so plan both: immediate mark + control plane kill; credits only if we detect overlap persisted > 2s.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: runtime/feature/resume-control -> canary(us-east) at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z.

maria: Thanks. Let's sync after the canary run and decide whether to promote.

jin: I'll post a short runbook in #eng-runtime with how to reproduce locally and the new logs to look for.

kevin: I'll add a console QA checklist (show badge, link traces, no perf regression).

olivia: Adding runbook tests to CI to catch this class of issue.

maria: Great work team. :thumbsup:
